digest.component_or_area: store sync and push union guards
propositions: A stale clone with mismatched epoch silently re-unions stripped history (~1 GiB) at two independent sites (sync._union_merge and push.py non-FF retry) because merge-base succeeds on byte-identical pre-strip commits, bypassing unrelated-histories detection.

The epoch guard must be placed at both sync._union_merge (before merge, not before merge-base test) and in push.py (before non-FF retry merges), or a guard at either site alone is bypassed by independent control flow reaching the other site.

The epoch field lives in .store-compat.json as an opaque JSON string (ISO-8601 UTC instant plus random suffix); unknown keys are safely ignored by older binaries, and write_compat_record preserves but never generates an epoch value.

The full state matrix specifies behavior for all nine combinations of local/remote record and epoch presence/absence: only record-absent/record-absent, record-absent/epoch-absent, and equal epochs are compatible; all mismatches or corrupt records abort.

On epoch mismatch, sync._union_merge returns without merging (leaving clone un-converged), and push.py immediately returns from push_tickets_branch to abort retry loop (zero merges, zero further attempts), both emitting logger.warning; neither path silently retries.

A guard-aborted non-fast-forward push leaves both local and remote refs byte-identical, fsck reports DIVERGED (not PUSH_PENDING), and merely-behind or strictly-ahead clones with matching epochs still converge normally.
